sentences.text: Computer use is like hiring an assistant who works at the computer.
The agent looks at the screen and acts using vision and reasoning.
It is useful when a system has no A P I, only a screen.
It requires generative orchestration.
Think of it as a digital employee.
When you set it up, you enter a name, a description, a model, instructions, and the machine.
The instructions must include full addresses and explicit steps, as if you were explaining the job to someone who has never done it.
The clearer the steps, the better the agent works and the fewer mistakes it makes.
There are three places where it can run.
Hosted browser, in preview, is for experimenting.
Cloud PC pool, also in preview, uses machines joined to Entra and Intune.
And you can use your own machine with Power Automate for desktop.
Soon you will see which one fits production.
The maker's credentials are risky if the agent is shared.
It is better to use stored credentials, in internal storage or Azure Key Vault, or the end user's credentials.
Human supervision sends an Outlook email to a reviewer when it detects potentially harmful instructions.
The cost is five Copilot Credits per step with standard models and fifteen with premium models.
It is not included in the Microsoft three six five Copilot license.
And here is the trap: choosing Hosted browser for production, when it is only for experimenting.
Keep that in mind when you answer.
